narrative.overview:
**Creative North Star: "The Registered Plate"**

Clearhaul is set like a plate section in a printed design annual. The page is near-white uncoated stock, ink is near-black, and structure comes from one-pixel hairlines rather than boxes and shadows. The map is the plate: framed by a hairline, held by registration marks at its corners, and stamped with a periwinkle seal when a route is recommended. Everything a driver or dispatcher needs to decide sits in a single ruled column beside it.

The system is deliberately quiet so that risk can be loud. The base map is a near-monochrome grey, the interface is ink and paper, and the only strong colors on screen are the five risk levels. Density stays moderate: the verdict is the largest type on the page, supporting numbers sit in plain rows, and nothing competes with the answer.

The owner chose this world for a professional tool that must not look like a generic AI dashboard and must not be too dense to read.
keyCharacteristics: Near-white ground that drifts warm at the top left and cool at the bottom right, so it reads as paper rather than a flat fill.
One grotesque typeface for everything, with a monospace face only for labels and measures.
Square corners, one-pixel hairlines, and no decorative shadows.
Risk is the only strong color, and every risk level also has its own shape.
One authored motion: results settle into place once when a plan arrives.

rules.name: The Risk Owns Color Rule
rules.body: Strong color means risk. Interface chrome stays ink, hairline and paper; the periwinkle seal is the only other accent, and it only marks the current choice.

rules.name: The Shape Before Color Rule
rules.body: Every risk level is drawn with its own road-sign shape: circle for Low, yield triangle for Moderate, square for High, warning diamond for Severe, and a stop octagon with a white bar for No Travel. Color is never the only signal.

rules.name: The Blank Is Not Low Rule
rules.body: Where the forecast has no data, the map is left transparent and the legend says so. Missing weather is never painted with the Low color.

rules.name: The Mono For Measures Rule
rules.body: Monospace is only for labels, statuses and measured values. Sentences, headings and buttons with long text are never set in it.

rules.name: The One Heading Rule
rules.body: A view has one display-size heading, and it states the answer or the question. Everything else steps down to title or body.

rules.name: The Hairline Rule
rules.body: Group things with one-pixel rules and a single shared border. Never stack cards, and never add a shadow to something that does not float over the map.

dos: keep the verdict as the largest type on screen, in the display style.
pair every risk color with its shape, in the map, lists and legends.
frame the map as a plate with hairlines and registration marks.
use Seal Periwinkle only for the current choice and the recommendation stamp.
keep motion to state changes: results settle in once (220ms, from 40% opacity and 8px down), and a thin bar sweeps while a plan loads. Both stop under the reduced-motion setting.
donts: add color to the interface beyond ink, hairline, paper, the seal and the risk scale.
round corners on controls or containers.
use shadows except on content that floats over the map.
use monospace for headings or sentences.
add labels above headings, numbered section markers or icon-and-heading card grids.
animate anything on the forecast slider's path. Each step only swaps a prepared image.
